title: TypeScript SDK: polymorphic shape registry, runtime descriptors, and Zod/JSON-Schema hydration
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem statement:
Customers want a predictable, ergonomically typed TypeScript SDK that can emit structured output from models while supporting streaming and retries. Current typegen produces static discriminated unions, but we see gaps: (1) runtime identification of polymorphic shapes when fields are missing or arrive incrementally during streaming, (2) a lightweight registry to map model shape descriptors to Zod validators/JSON-Schema for server-side validation and playground tooling, and (3) retry semantics that preserve partially streamed structured outputs and rehydrate state after transient failures.

Goal:
Build a runtime polymorphic descriptor system + shape registry and integrate Zod/JSON-Schema hydration into the ts-sdk runtime and codegen so developers can: (A) register model output shapes (both codegen and manual), (B) validate/parse streaming chunks as they arrive (incremental validation), (C) deterministically resolve discriminators even when the discriminator field is emitted late, and (D) rerun retries with deterministic reassembly of partial output and replay of validators.

Design highlights and constraints:
- Shape registry: runtime map from stable descriptor id -> parser + Zod schema + JSON-Schema. Registry supports lazy hydration (load schema on demand) and versioned descriptors so we can fallback to older validators when model rollouts occur.
- Descriptor: small JSON-compatible metadata blob emitted by codegen (descriptor id, candidate discriminators, fallback score heuristics, schema location). Codegen will include descriptor metadata alongside generated TypeScript types.
- Streaming parser: incremental buffer that feeds Zod-safe parsing checkpoints. We treat streaming tokens as appended text and attempt to extract top-level JSON chunks when they become valid. For partial objects, we run a lightweight structural checklist to narrow candidate shapes before full validation.
- Discriminator resolution: when discriminator key arrives late, registry performs a two-phase match: structural narrowing (shape keys present/absent) -> discriminator field check -> statistical fallback (model-supplied shape hint or classifier). This reduces premature misclassification and avoids silent schema errors.
- Retry semantics: on transient errors we persist the streaming buffer and registry decisions in the call context (opaque token) so retries (either automatic or manual) can resume parsing without forcing the application to re-prompt or lose partial outputs.

Acceptance criteria:
- Runtime registry implemented in ts-sdk runtime with API: registerDescriptor(id, zodSchema, jsonSchema?, metadata?) and resolveDescriptorFromPartial(objOrTokens).
- Codegen emits descriptor metadata files alongside type files and a small runtime binding that registers descriptors at module import time for static builds.
- Streaming parser can successfully validate and return a typed union value for 3 canonical test prompts where discriminator appears at: (a) beginning, (b) middle, (c) end of stream.
- Retry replay test where connection drops after 40% tokens: retry returns the same typed output and does not double-emit side-effects (idempotency test harness).
- Documentation + examples: playground snippet demonstrating registerDescriptor, streamingParseWithRegistry, and retryResume.

Risks & trade-offs:
- Registry increases the runtime surface area and bundle size. Mitigation: make hydration optional and lazy; codegen can emit minimal inline descriptors for small models and external JSON manifest for large catalogs.
- Zod parsing on every streaming checkpoint could be expensive. Mitigation: use a short-circuit structural checklist and only run full parse when candidate set is small or end-of-object detected.
- Complexity around versioning descriptors across model rollouts. Mitigation: include descriptor version in codegen and allow a fallback chain; Platform routing may auto-fall back to compatible model variant where descriptor mismatch is detected.

Engineering tasks (high level):
1) Core runtime registry + descriptor API (register/lookup/versioned fallback)
2) Streaming incremental parser + structural narrowing heuristics
3) Codegen changes: emit descriptor metadata alongside types and a registration shim
4) Zod/JSON-Schema adapters (hydration + lazy fetch for external manifests)
5) Retry integration: persist/restore streaming buffer + registry state in retry token
6) Tests: unit, integration (streaming cases), e2e retry replay tests, performance microbenchmarks
7) Docs/examples + playground notebook

comments: 2025-02-13 - Sofia: Initial scoping and prototype spike completed. Verified that a small registry (<= 10 descriptors) adds ~12kb gzipped to the runtime when descriptors are inlined; external manifest reduces this to ~3kb but adds a network fetch. Decision: support both inlined and manifest modes.

2025-02-19 - Liam: Implemented first pass of registerDescriptor API and a naive streaming JSON assembler. Added unit tests for simple discriminator-first streams. Filed follow-up ENG-208402 for making registry lazy-load manifest. Linking PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1423

2025-02-25 - PM review (Aria Chen): Requested clearer UX for codegen: prefer module-level auto-registration shim for DX and a manual register api for bundle-sensitive apps. Also flagged acceptance criteria for retry idempotency tests.

2025-02-28 - Design review (Noah Kim): Suggested structural-checklist heuristics to reduce Zod runs — we should check key fingerprints and lengths before running full validators. Noah also suggested adding a numeric "shape-score" to descriptors to help fallback ranking.

2025-03-03 - Liam: Added streaming middle/discriminator-late testcases and updated parser to run lightweight checks. Performance microbenchmarks show ~18% CPU overhead on worst-case 4k token streams with full-parse-on-every-checkpoint; we will gate full-parse behind structural narrowing to avoid this in stable builds.

2025-03-05 - Sofia: Merged streaming parser and registry into feature branch. Next: extend codegen to emit descriptor metadata and add playground example for retryResume. Planning follow-up tasks: ENG-208409 (codegen emitter), ENG-208410 (retry token persistence), ENG-208411 (docs + examples).
acceptance_criteria: Runtime registry API implemented and documented
Codegen emits descriptor metadata and registration shim
Streaming parsing validates and returns typed union for canonical cases
Retry replay preserves partial buffer and returns deterministic typed output
Examples and playground demonstrating the end-to-end flow
